subject: Agriculture
title: Blockchain in Food Supply
description: Learn Blockchain in Food Supply in one minute.

hook.text: Walmart traces mangoes from farm to store in 2.2 seconds using blockchain. Before, it took seven days.

buildup.text: Food fraud costs $40 billion annually. Olive oil, honey, and fish are among the most commonly faked foods.

discovery.text: Blockchain creates an immutable record of every step in the supply chain—farm, processor, shipper, retailer.

twist.text: Blockchain only records what people enter. If someone lies at the farm gate, the chain of blocks records a lie.

climax.text: IBM Food Trust and similar platforms are being adopted by Nestlé, Carrefour, and Dole for supply chain transparency.

punchline.text: Blockchain trusts no one—that's the point. But it can't verify what happens off-screen.

quiz.question: How fast can Walmart trace mangoes using blockchain?

details.summary: Blockchain in food supply chains creates tamper-proof digital records that trace food from farm to fork. This topic covers how distributed ledger technology improves transparency, speeds up food safety recalls, and builds consumer trust in sourcing claims.
details.whyItMatters: Foodborne illness outbreaks cost billions and take days to trace. Blockchain can reduce traceback time from weeks to seconds, saving lives and reducing food waste during recalls.
takeaways: Walmart traced mangoes from store to farm in 2.2 seconds using blockchain
Each supply chain participant adds verified data to an immutable shared ledger
Blockchain helps verify organic, fair-trade, and origin claims against fraud

faq.question: How is blockchain used in the food supply chain?
faq.answer: Each participant—farmer, processor, distributor, retailer—records transaction and handling data on a shared, tamper-proof digital ledger. This creates an unbroken chain of custody that anyone can verify, from harvest to supermarket shelf.

faq.question: What problems does blockchain solve in food traceability?
faq.answer: Blockchain eliminates paper-based record gaps, reduces traceback time during food safety emergencies from days to seconds, prevents fraudulent origin or certification claims, and gives consumers verifiable transparency about their food.
